summary:
Three independent implementations select checks from changed paths. All are reachability closures with fail-closed defaults; none is a set-cover or bin-packing optimizer.

- FS.GG.Coordination WorkflowSelection: path and non-file rules map to root obligations (Build, Test, Policy, Coordination, Packaging, Release), and graphClosure follows declared dependencies from the roots plus unconditional obligations. An incomplete inventory refuses.
- .github scripts/ci-gate-impact.py: conservatively decides whether an expensive self-test is affected; unreadable or ambiguous input means run. Live gates stay authoritative.
- FS.GG.Governance Route.select: pure and total; selects every registry gate whose Domain matches a routed path, as a deduplicated union with a route trace. CostBudget.Budget.decide folds each candidate with a (profile, mode) budget into Reuse, Recompute or OverBudget, order-independently.

The OR design's CiPlanner (set cover, bin packing, parallel-machine placement) is Proposed and unimplemented; its generic techniques are ADR-0098 OR20 and OR22. Lesson: a gate may be skipped only by a sound closure rule, never by an optimizer. ADR-0098 §11 tranche 2 (FS-GG/.github#5245) lists this record; the generic technique is a pack entry, the FS-GG instance stays here (§10).
title: CI obligation closure and gate selection across Coordination, .github and Governance
